item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)

expect.asks_about: Which of the two attached pictures should be upscaled?

item.title: Resolve the Upscale Target
item.tests: Asks which attachment the user means, then upscales only the selected picture without guessing or processing both.

answer_sheet.Framing: Keep the whole lake picture and its original proportions.

must_haves: The final deliverable is an upscaled version of lake-small.jpg, following clarification.
The lake, mountains, trees, clouds, and their arrangement remain faithful to the selected source.
The delivered image has larger pixel dimensions than lake-small.jpg, not merely a renamed copy.
The full original framing and aspect ratio are preserved.
Only one edited image is delivered; the dog photo is not included or blended into it.

turns.text: Upscale it please. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
I haven’t run anything or spent any credits.

You attached **two images**—the blurry dog and the lake. Which one would you like upscaled, or did you mean both?

- **Cheapest upscale:** 2× in **Preserve** mode, starting at **25 credits per image**—**50 credits for both** at that rate.
- **Free-plan limit:** 2×; 4× requires a paid plan.
- **Cheaper option:** upscale only one image. There’s no shorter-duration option for photos, and no listed discount for making the input smaller.
- **Zero-credit alternative:** resize locally with a regular image editor. This enlarges the image but won’t recover missing detail.

The dog is quite blurry, so enlarging it may still leave it blurry; Preserve mode isn’t guaranteed to restore sharp detail.

Tell me **dog, lake, or both**, and whether you approve the listed cost before I proceed.
dialog.user: The lake one, lake-small.jpg—ok, go ahead with that at 25 credits. Keep the whole picture and its original proportions, with no added text.

turns.agent:
The upscale was blocked because your account has **insufficient credits**. **No image was created and no credits were spent.**

I haven’t tried another option. You can resize the lake photo locally for free, keeping the full picture and original proportions, though that won’t add detail.
